correctness.rationale: The Picard intersection model explicitly generates all 56 exceptional classes and 576 seven-curve disjoint sets, with seven integral reflections. Fully enumerating 2,903,040 distinct group elements, partitioning by conjugacy into 60 classes, then computing one exact 576-cycle decomposition per class gives the exhaustive nine-value spectrum, not an extrapolation. The independent witness script checks the exceptional 56, 576, 288 profiles and Geiser commute relation. The published 2018 Loughran–Trepalin theorem guarantees the extremal Weyl class occurs over every odd q≥9. Pairwise disjoint Galois-stable exceptional curves admit a contraction to a Severi–Brauer surface split over finite fields.

originality.rationale: Published work supplies the classical 56 exceptional curves, 288 Aronhold markings, W(E7) Frobenius types, and finite-field realizations. The new claim is instead the exact nine-value minimum-extension-degree spectrum for the 576 Galois-acted unordered seven-curve contraction sets, and a certified order-eighteen class in which degree-nine heptads fail to lift to a degree-nine plane contraction. Main relevant papers were compared at the level of statements and implications. No inspected primary text or indexed result states this complete 576-set orbit minimum; historical priority remains a risk rather than a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An older unindexed permutation-character table for the 576 blowdown markings could contain the equivalent evaluated minimum-orbit spectrum.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural field-of-definition invariant of actual plane blowdown morphisms, not merely a formal statistic: it gives the uniform sharp extension degree 18, all nine possible degrees, and exhibits a structural quadratic obstruction when a degree-nine Aronhold heptad has no degree-nine contraction lift. This matters for constructing explicit birational models and separating geometric and arithmetic markings. Its relevance is not contingent on unproved downstream theorems.
